43e55f2c.text:
You dial yourself up every morning.

The switch says: what is that hum?

I’m calling for myself. The humming is not my own,

726f0c19.text: it is the noise of the machine.

e420caf1.text: I am a machine. I am a telephone line.

ac6edf99.text: And in this room there are all sorts of voices,

0e3248d7.text: all the time. You know, they’re all talking.

c9e2bbde.text: I don’t mind, just as long as there is one left in the room.

4b19bf0c.text: One voice left in the room. There is a humming sound.

fed6f6f4.text: The machine is a phone line.

d16699d3.text: You can tell because it keeps ringing,

b60c8868.text: it rings so frequently. But when the machine rings,

f5b4f7a7.text: and there is nobody at the other end, then that’s when you hear

ed73527c.text: the voice of the telephone line.

c2f97f1a.text: It is a humming noise, like somebody with an out of tune violin,

98d7eeb4.text: and I have no choice but to pick up.

79e6d9a4.text: So it is you? You’ll call me?

e016059a.text: But it will be like this? This way? Every morning?

b4747c0b.text: Maybe the machine will ring and ring.

84c40dc0.text: Maybe I’ll just sit here in this chair.

472e439b.text: Maybe I’ll look at myself in this mirror

7ca2841f.text: and I won’t see myself at all, not a face or a body or a name,

4cde61b5.text: some kind of thing, a kind of noise, a kind of noise,
